title: Miscellaneous comments using “particular”
summary: This topic is loosely clustered around fragments containing “particular,” mixing sparse comments about comfort, features, handling, and cases where customers said nothing specific.

positive.summary: The positive example is a generic prompt about what the customer liked and does not provide a concrete vehicle aspect beyond asking for a particular favorite.

negative.summary: Negative feedback centers on comfort and ergonomics, including a seat belt rubbing the neck and an example labeled negative that actually states nothing was missing from the chosen package.

undetermined.summary: Undetermined fragments include vague or incomplete mentions, unspecified responses of nothing in particular, a request for simpler map-light control, praise of handling, and an access issue involving the A-pillar.

limitations: The topic is lexically driven by the word “particular” and mixes unrelated subjects rather than a single coherent customer issue.
Several fragments are too vague, incomplete, or framed as interviewer prompts, which limits reliable interpretation of customer sentiment and aspect-level themes.
One fragment assigned negative describes satisfaction with the selected package, so the supplied sentiment labels and fragment wording do not always align.
